title: Console: Dehydrate Mode — prune telemetry surface and on-demand cost detail
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Propose an intentional scope cut called 'Dehydrate Mode' for the Console MVP to meet launch time and cost targets. Dehydrate Mode reduces telemetry surface area by turning most route-level cost breakdown cards into on-demand expansions, enabling aggressive trace sampling defaults, and replacing heavy cross-route joins with lightweight rollup counts. This ticket captures PRD-level decisions, clarifying requirements for what remains visible by default, fallback behaviors, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating.

Why: The full insights surface exceeds current telemetry budget and risks delaying the release due to backend instrumentation and storage costs. Dehydrate Mode enables an acceptable product experience for early customers while preserving upgrade paths to the full insights surface in later cycles.

Scope changes (what is removed from default MVP surface):
- Remove per-route hourly cost heatmap; replace with single top-line route cost metric and a 90-day sparklines row.
- Collapse full token-level cost breakdown card into a single summary with an "Expand" action that fetches detailed rows on demand.
- Default trace capture: sample 1% for low-traffic routes, 10% for high-error/high-latency routes. Full traces are available via "Request traces" button with a soft quota.
- Disable route-level request-level event logs by default; keep aggregated counts (200/500/timeout) and surface error examples sampled.
- Remove cross-route cost joins for MVP (cost attribution by user/project will be a Dedicated-only follow-up).

What stays in the MVP surface (minimal but actionable):
- Route list with: requests/min, p95 latency, error rate, approximate token cost per 1k requests, and a 7-day sparkline.
- Cost overview top card with daily spend, 7-day trend, and quick breakdown by model family (hosted/dedicated) aggregated.
- Search and route filter by name, team, model, and SLA tier (supports quick incident triage).

Telemetry UX clarifications:
- Expand actions must be rate-limited in the UI (max 3 expands per minute per user) and fall back to a cached summary if backend is overloaded.
- Dehydrate Mode will be opt-out for add-on customers (Dedicated/Enterprise) by default opt-in for early access.

Engineering constraints and trade-offs: backend storage cost saved by replacing continuous per-request logs with a hybrid cached aggregation and on-demand fetch. This increases latency for the first expand action for a route; acceptable trade-off given improved release velocity. We will instrument metrics for expand latency and failure rate to determine when to rehydrate.

Rollout plan and gating:
- Feature flag: console.dehydrate_mode.enabled (default: true for public hosted free-tier, false for enterprise by default).
- Canary cohort: 5% of new signups, and internal Redwood customers. Monitor expand-success rate >= 95% and average expand latency <= 2.5s before 50% ramp.
- Gate to full enable when backend storage delta projected < 20% of current budget or expand error rate < 3% for two weeks.

Engineering artifacts and links:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/Console/PRD-Dehydrate-Mode (draft)
- Design mockups for summary vs expanded cards: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/designs/dehydrate-cards.png
- Initial backend design doc: https://wiki.redwood.ai/infra/dehydrate-mode-arch
- GitHub spike PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8912 and /pull/8950

Notes from cross-functional sync (3/05):
- Design: use microcopy to set expectations when showing sampled traces and on-demand fetches.
- Eng: need a lightweight aggregation API (ENG-20211) and expand fetch API (ENG-20577).
- Security: no additional PI stored in expanded rows; expanded fetch enforces ACL check per request.

Acceptance criteria (quantified where possible):
acceptance_criteria: Default Console launch shows Dehydrate Mode summary surface with no per-route hourly heatmaps and no continuous per-request logs.
Expand action returns detailed cost rows within 3s p95 for 95% of requests during normal load and <5% error rate in canary cohort.
Top-level cost card accurately reflects daily spend within 5% of billing exports for 7 consecutive days post-launch.
Trace sampling obeys policy: <=1% sample for low-traffic routes and >=10% for high-error routes; verify via synthetic traffic checks (ENG test harness).
Feature flagging and rollout gating implemented; ability to disable Dehydrate Mode globally within 30 minutes of toggling the flag.
Design microcopy and tooltips in place explaining "on-demand" expands and sampling to reduce support tickets; copy reviewed by design and content and included in initial release.
Operational dashboards created: expand_latency, expand_error_rate, dehydrate_enabled_percent, and daily_telemetry_storage_bytes.
decision_record: Adopt Dehydrate Mode as an MVP cut to balance telemetry costs and time-to-market; prioritize expandable details over full always-on surface. Rehydrate progression gated on storage delta and expand SLA metrics.
updates: 2026-03-03: PM sync — confirmed backend API surface (ENG-20211, ENG-20577).
2026-03-05: Design review — microcopy and minimal animation for expand state approved by DES-9123.
2026-03-09: Risks logged — potential support spike from customers who expect always-on breakdowns; support playbook drafted.
2026-03-10: Updated acceptance criteria to include operational dashboards and quantitative expand SLA.
